lib.release — pack and push .NET projects in a repository to nuget.org.

GETTING STARTED (in a target repo)
  1. lib.release --check <dir>   Verify the repo is compatible and see what would be released.
  2. lib.release --init  <dir>   Create lib.release.json (greedily includes every releasable project + test).
  3. lib.release --schema        Print the lib.release.json JSON Schema (the full field contract).
  4. Review versions in lib.release.json, commit, then release:
     lib.release <dir> --ApiKey <key>

RELEASE USAGE
  lib.release <Lib> [--ApiKey <key>] [--SkipTests] [-v|-d]

  <Lib>          Target repo: a rooted path, or a bare name resolved under
                 LIB_RELEASE_PROJECTS_DIR (default c:\projects).
  --ApiKey <k>   nuget.org push key. Falls back to the NUGET_API_KEY env var.
  --SkipTests    Skip the test step.
  -v|--verbose   Verbose (trace) logging.    -d|--debug  Debug logging.

MODES (no API key required, non-interactive)
  --check [dir]  Pre-flight compatibility report (read-only). Default dir: current directory.
  --init  <dir>  Scaffold lib.release.json into <dir>. Greedy: includes every releasable project and
                 every test project found. Overrides:
                   --exclude <names>  comma/space-separated project names to leave out
                   --force            overwrite an existing lib.release.json
  --migrate <dir>  Convert a legacy (name-based) lib.release.json to the path-based format in place,
                   preserving versions. Writes nothing unless every entry resolves to a real csproj.
  --schema       Print the embedded JSON Schema for lib.release.json.
  -h|--help|-?   This help.

THE MANIFEST (lib.release.json, at the repo root)
  releases[]  one per package:  { "project" (path to .csproj), "version" (M.m.p), "prerelease" }
  tests[]     paths to test-project .csproj files to run before packing
  Projects are referenced by .csproj path relative to the repo root (e.g.
  "src/Foo/Foo.csproj"); no naming/layout convention. The package id comes from
